- The failing test expects an early `NumberIsTooLargeException` when the bounds range is so large that normalization would overflow.
- Static inspection shows `checkParameters()` detects finite vs infinite bounds, but after storing finite bounds it only contains a comment:

- `FitnessFunction.encode(double[])` later computes:

  - `res[i] = (x[i] - lower) / diff`

- `upper - lower` overflows to `Infinity`
- `0 - lower` also overflows to `Infinity`
- so encoding becomes `Infinity / Infinity = NaN`

That `NaN` is passed to the objective, which intentionally throws `MathIllegalStateException`, matching the observed failure.

So the root cause is:
- missing overflow-range validation in `checkParameters()`
- symptom manifests later in `FitnessFunction.encode(double[])`

The method that should have rejected this case is `CMAESOptimizer.checkParameters()`.

m23.content:
The bug is in `CMAESOptimizer.checkParameters()`.

Why:
- The failing test expects an early `NumberIsTooLargeException` when the bounds range is so large that normalization would overflow.
- Static inspection shows `checkParameters()` detects finite vs infinite bounds, but after storing finite bounds it only contains a comment:

  > `// Abort early if the normalization will overflow (cf. "encode" method).`

  and performs no actual check.

- `FitnessFunction.encode(double[])` later computes:
  - `diff = upper - lower`
  - `res[i] = (x[i] - lower) / diff`

For the test values:
- `lower = -tooLarge`
- `upper = tooLarge`
- `start = 0`

Then:
- `upper - lower` overflows to `Infinity`
- `0 - lower` also overflows to `Infinity`
- so encoding becomes `Infinity / Infinity = NaN`

That `NaN` is passed to the objective, which intentionally throws `MathIllegalStateException`, matching the observed failure.

So the root cause is:
- missing overflow-range validation in `checkParameters()`
- symptom manifests later in `FitnessFunction.encode(double[])`

The method that should have rejected this case is `CMAESOptimizer.checkParameters()`.
